 3                             I.    OVERVIEW OF TESTIMONY

 4     Q.   ARE YOU THE SAME FREDERICK B. WULFF, JR. ("FRED") THAT FILED

 5          INTERVENOR DIRECT TESTIMONY IN THIS DOCKET ON BEHALF OF

 6          WULFF BLUFF CREEK RANCH, LTD., FOUND AT INTERCHANGE (4441)?

 7     A.   Yes

 8     Q.   WHAT        HAVE        YOU   DONE     TO    PREPARE        THIS     CROSS-REBUTTAL

 9          TESTIMONY?

10     A.   I have reviewed the Intervenor Direct Testimonies referred to herein, as well as many other

11          testimonies. I cannot say I have reviewed all the Intervenor Direct Testimonies filed in this

12          case.
13     Q.   WHAT QUALIFIES YOU TO GIVE THIS TESTIMONY?

14     A.   Please see my overall list of relevant experience in my direct testimony. To summarize, I

15          have extensive education and professional experience in large-scale and geographic data

16          analysis.

17                  Since my direct testimony did not involve as much aviation and topographic work

18          as this submission does, I additionally note that part of my work as a Software Engineer at

19          Google was on elevation data - in particular, contributing to the software architecture used

20          for 3D building rendering. Since then, I have used elevation data for multiple professional

21          products and am familiar with its representation and processing. The FAA uses a

22          standardized format for aviation elevation data that I have worked with extensively.

23     Q.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

24     A.   I am testifying to rebut two categories of testimony raised by various intervenors that do

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                         2         CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF
     SOAHDOCKET 473-26-16349                                      FREDERICK B. WULFF, JR.
  1                    not hold up to geographic or data analysis.

 2                            The first category oftestimony is focused on airstrips and airports. There are several

 3                    intervenors who either introduce new grass airstrips not included in the analysis or raise

 4                    concerns about the effects of proposed links on Curtis Field, an existing airport owned by

 5                    the City ofBrady. I provide geographic analysis of the mentioned airstrips along Route 392,

 6                    showing that the concerns are not credible, and I provide analysis showing that link V8 is

 7                    compatible with Curtis Field.

 8                            The second category of testimony consists of experts providing end-to-end

 9                    quantitative assessments of routes. For reasons initially raised in my direct testimony, I

10                    believe that analysis based primarily on Applicants' "apparent" property boundaries and

11                    cost estimation philosophy are fundamentally flawed. I offer more additional analysis and

12                    a mapping tool in response to certain Intervenor Direct Testimonies demonstrating why

13                    Route 392 is still the best available routing choice.

14                                           II.   CURTIS FIELD AIRPORT

15           Q.       WHAT FAA DATA DID YOU REVIEW IN PREPARATION FOR REBUTTING

16                    CONCERNS AROUND AIRPORTS AND AIRSTRIPS?

17           A.       The FAA produces geographic data delineating airport obstacle surfaces (i.e. the elevation

18                    at which an object is considered an "obstacle" by the FAA) as part of its Obstruction

19                    Evaluation/Airport      Airspace     Analysis     (OE3A)      program 1.    Since    FAA     elevation

20                    requirements are based on the elevation of the airport runway and may vary with terrain, I

21                    downloaded this data and combined it with the USGS 1/9 arc second elevation DEM

22                    dataseti I then mapped the area where the obstacle surface was less than 170 feet off the

  1                    ground, using the maximum "typical" height submitted by applicants, accounting for terrain

 2                    elevation changes.

 3                              I also reviewed current and histoiical satellite photography of mentioned airstrips3, as

 4                    well as FAA OE3A public records for requests for airstrip and obstacle determinations.

 5            Q.     WHAT CONCERNS DID INTERVENORS RAISE AROUND CURTIS FIELD, THE

 6                   CITY OF BRADY'S MUNICIPAL AIRPORT?

 7            A.      Intervenors raised several concerns that the planned V8 link might impact Curtis Field's

 8                    current or planned operations. None of the intervenors that I reviewed claim to have

 9                    personal aviation experience or expertise. The two most distinctive testimonies are those of

10                    City ofBrady City Manager James Stewart (Item 4435) and Matt and Suzzette McBee (Item

11                    4045), so I rebut them directly. Others echo the same concerns with less specificity.

12            Q.     WHAT IS YOUR ANALYSIS OF MR. STEWART'S CONCERNS ON BEHALF OF

13                   THE CITY OF BRADY?

14            A.      While Mr. Stewart filed his testimony in his official capacity as City Manager, I note two

15                    flaws with his testimony insomuch as the Commission would consider it as an official

16                    statement of the City and as such give it increased deference as a reflection of Community

17                    Values.

18                              First, despite Mr. Stewart's wide-ranging testimony, the agenda item 4 for the

19                    resolution enabling intervention passed by the Brady City Council in their May 5 meeting

20                    contained only the following explanation ofthe City' s concerns: "One ofthe routes crosses

21                    near the airport that could prohibit expansion. The City desires to protect its interest in the

22                    airport' s future and desires to intervene." The agenda item contained only a single page of

  1          Applicants' notice map, which depicted only the V and U links in the neighborhood of

 2          Richland Springs and Rochelle, notably omitting the portion of V8 nearest Curtis Field.

 3                  As a result, there seems to be no official record that the Council properly considered

 4          any concrete expansion plans for Curtis Field, conducted a holistic comparison with other

 5          links such Mll that also go near the City, or even was aware of the actual path of proposed

 6          link V8 near Curtis Field.

 7                  Second, to the extent that Mr. Stewart's conversion of Council' s the general desire

 8          to protect expansion opportunities into "adding 500 feet more in length" to the runway is

 9          due to unstated knowledge of more concrete short-term plans obtained in his position as

10          City Manager, there are two fundamental issues. First, there is no explanation for whether

11          the expansion would be on the northern end or the southern end of the runway. If the

12          southern end, then it would have no effect on the clearance requirements on the northern

13          end, since clearance requirements are computed from each runway end independently. An

14          expansion to the south would make no difference vis a vis this project, since link V8 is after

15          all north of the airport.

16                  As to a potential northerly runway expansion, my analysis shows that expanding the

17          northern end by 500 feet could theoretically introduce a modest conflict resolvable by

18          shortening the relevant towers by <10 feet, but such a northern expansion seems unlikely

19          since per the McCulloch County Appraisal District data, there is only 383 feet between the

20          northern end of the runway and the northern edge of the City of Brady' s property boundary.

21          In other words, such an expansion would not only be a speculative future use of the City's

22          property but would also require property beyond that currently owned by the City.

 3     Q.     WHAT QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS DID YOU CONDUCT ON THE ROUTING

 4            ARGUMENTS?

 5     A.     My primary focus on my initial pass was to establish a principled analytic framework

 6            supported by real-world data for comparing the expert recommendations. This had two

 7            main components.

 8                   First, since many experts focused their discussion on either the western section of the

 9            routes or the eastern section of the routes. All the exemplar routes recommended by the

10            experts mentioned above utilize link G73. Using the same link allows independently

11            comparing the eastern and western portions of the routes.

12                    Second, I reviewed each route portion for the issues that Dr. Turnbough, Dr.

13            Rhodes, and myself identified in our direct testimonies. In particular, I examined the
